files.content:
# Maintenance mode (block: maintenance)

Maintenance and read-only mode switched at runtime by admins: stored in MongoDB and cached briefly so every instance agrees, 503 with Retry-After and a message, reads kept in read-only mode, scheduled windows, an allowlist (admins, IPs, sign-in, health checks, devtools), a public status route for banners, and an env override for deploys.

The code is in `app/blocks/maintenance/` and belongs to this project. Options go in `calm.config.js` under `blocks['maintenance']`; secrets go in `.env`.

## For AI agents

- Read `app/blocks/maintenance/index.js` first: the header lists routes, what is let through and how instances agree.
- Options live in `calm.config.js` under `blocks.maintenance`; the runtime state lives in the `calm_maintenance` collection (one document, `_id: 'state'`).
- Enforcement is one `calm.guard` with `order: -100`, so it runs before every other guard. Keep it first, and keep it cheap: it reads the cached state, never MongoDB per request.
- Windows are evaluated against the clock on every request (`effective()`); only the stored document is cached (`cacheMs`). Do not cache the computed mode.
- Read-only mode lets GET, HEAD and OPTIONS through and refuses everything else; routes that write on GET are your bug, not the block's.
- Always allowed: `GET /maintenance`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/logout`, plus `options.allow` ('METHOD /path' without /api). Admins pass by `bypassRoles`.
- IP allowlists compare `req.ip`, which depends on `config.trustProxy` (TRUST_PROXY). Behind a load balancer set it, or every client shares the proxy's address.
- `/health/*` and devtools are mounted before the API router and are never blocked; do not move them behind it.
- `MAINTENANCE_MODE` (env) overrides the stored state and needs no database; doctor reports it while set.
- From code: `app.ext.maintenance.set({ mode: 'read-only', until })` and `await app.ext.maintenance.status()`.
- Events: `maintenance.changed` with the new state and who changed it.

## Official documentation

- [RFC 9110: 503 Service Unavailable](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-503-service-unavailable)
- [RFC 9110: Retry-After](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-retry-after)
- [MDN: 503 Service Unavailable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/503)
- [Express: behind proxies (req.ip and trust proxy)](https://expressjs.com/en/guide/behind-proxies.html)
- [MongoDB update operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/update/)

## Usage

Admins: PATCH /api/admin/maintenance { mode: 'maintenance' | 'read-only' | 'off', message?, retryAfterSeconds?, until?, allowIps? }; POST /api/admin/maintenance/windows { start, end, mode?, message? }; DELETE /api/admin/maintenance/windows/:id; GET /api/admin/maintenance.
Everyone: GET /api/maintenance -> { mode, message, until, retryAfterSeconds, upcoming } for banners.
Blocked requests get 503 MAINTENANCE (or READ_ONLY for writes) with Retry-After. Admins, allowlisted IPs, sign-in, /health/* and devtools pass.
MAINTENANCE_MODE=maintenance|read-only in .env forces a mode without the database. Options (blocks.maintenance): cacheMs, retryAfterSeconds, message, readOnlyMessage, allowIps, bypassRoles, allow.

## Environment variables

- `MAINTENANCE_MODE`

More: https://docs.calmapi.dev/blocks/maintenance
